title: Pumpkin Chicken Curry
ingredients: 3.5 lbs (approx. 1.6 kg) skinless boneless chicken breast, cut into bite-sized chunks
1/2 cup canned full-fat coconut milk (replaces yogurt)
2 2/3 tsp Kashmiri chili powder (or regular mild chili powder)
1 to 1 1/2 cups canned full-fat coconut milk (divided for cooking & finishing)
1 tsp Kashmiri chili powder (optional, for extra heat)
1 tsp fine sea salt (or to taste)
2 tsp sugar or maple syrup (optional, to balance flavor)
1-2 tbsp fresh lime juice (recommended to replicate yogurt's acidity)
instructions: Marinate the chicken: In a large bowl, whisk together 1/2 cup coconut milk, 2 tbsp oil, 5 tsp curry powder, 2 2/3 tsp chili powder, 1 1/3 tsp garlic powder, 1 1/3 tsp onion powder, and 1 1/3 tsp salt. Add chicken chunks, coat well, cover, and refrigerate for 20-30 minutes.

Bloom the spices: Heat 2 tbsp vegetable oil in a large pot over low-medium heat. Add the dry spice powders for the sauce (onion powder, garlic powder, ground ginger, garam masala, curry powder, and optional chili powder). Stir constantly for 30-60 seconds until fragrant (watch closely so the dry spices don't burn).

Build the sauce: Immediately stir in the pumpkin puree, tomato paste, water (or broth), and 1 tsp salt. Whisk until smooth, cover, and let simmer gently on low heat for 8-10 minutes. Stir in the sugar/maple syrup and 1 cup of coconut milk. Remove from heat briefly.
Sear the chicken: Heat a large skillet over medium-high heat. In 2-3 batches (to avoid overcrowding), sear the marinated chicken chunks for 2-3 minutes until lightly browned on the outside.
Simmer together: Transfer the seared chicken into the warm pumpkin curry sauce. Cover and simmer on low heat for 4-5 minutes until the chicken is cooked through.
Finish: Turn off the heat and stir in the remaining coconut milk and fresh lime juice. Adjust salt to taste and serve hot over rice or naan.
notes: Nutrition per serving (1 of 8), dish only without cooked rice. Also provides 10 g saturated fat and 105 mg cholesterol.
